newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says EMU debate damages euro project.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says EMU debate damages euro project.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Thursday the continuing debate about the criteria for Europe's single currency was damaging for economic and monetary union (EMU).

Waigel told journalists that taking a loose interpretation of the Maastricht budget target -- three percent of gross domestic product (GDP) -- could lead to countries ending up with deficits as high as 3.9 percent.
Waigel said the convergence of economies joining the EMU was more important than the project's timetable, which foresees the launch of the euro in 1999.
Speculation about an EMU delay was also damaging to the project, he added.

Waigel said Bonn, now considering revaluing Bundesbank gold and currency reserces and selling off some of its Deutsche Telekom shares to help fill holes in its budget, would force the pace of privatisation in the next two years.
The minister also said he expected stronger growth, higher tax revenues and lower unemployment levels next year.
